name: expandable-gallery

frames.best_why: Frame 5 shows one photo panel stretched noticeably wider than its four neighbours.

tagline: Photo panels sit in a row and widen under the pointer.
summary: A row of equally sized image panels fills the width. Hovering one lets it grow to three times its share while the others narrow, with a slow ease.
appearance: Five tall nature photos sit edge to edge in a single rounded row, each the same width. A small caption sits above, and hovering one stretches it wide while the rest squeeze thinner.
behaviour: At rest the panels share the row equally. On hover the pointed panel grows and its neighbours shrink, easing over half a second; moving away restores the even split.
demo_content: Five landscape photos: mountain sunrise, misty valley, forest, green meadow and a wooden bridge.
search_phrases: photo panels that grow on hover
use_when: A page wants a compact row of images where one can be previewed larger on hover.
avoid_when: Hover is the only trigger, so touch and keyboard users cannot expand a panel.
customise: images (URLs) and className are the only props; the fixed height, gap and three-times hover growth are in the source.
weight_why: Five image panels with a single CSS flex transition; no script.

a11y.note: Panels expand on hover only, so keyboard and touch users get no enlargement, and alt text is just the URL.

issues: Alt text on each photo is the raw image URL.
polish_why: Clean photo row and a smooth width change, but it is a thin, standard concept.
